title: Exact electrical identities, realized in real devices
question: How did quantum electrical standards move from 1990 conventional values to exact post-2019 International System of Units (SI) relationships without making laboratory realizations uncertainty-free?
answerPreview: Fixed h and e make K_J = 2e/h and R_K = h/e^2 exact SI relationships, while Josephson and quantum Hall devices remain practical realizations with operating conditions and uncertainty; K_J-90 and R_K-90 belong to a separate historical convention.
summary: Trace fixed h and e through exact Josephson, von Klitzing, conductance, flux, charge, and electron-volt identities; compare the historical 1990 conventional values without substituting them for current SI or practical realization results.

observationStage.title: Current SI anchors and the historical conventional layer
observationStage.question: Which values are current exact SI inputs, and which values were adopted as a historical practical convention?

items.label: Planck constant
items.explanation: The present SI fixes h exactly; it is an input to exact current relationships for K_J, R_K, G_0, and the superconducting flux quantum.

items.label: Elementary charge
items.explanation: The present SI fixes e exactly; it anchors charge and the exact joule value of one electron volt.

items.label: 1990 conventional Josephson constant K_J-90
items.explanation: This CIPM 1988 conventional value was used from 1990 for practical voltage representations; it is historical and is not the current exact SI value of K_J.

items.label: 1990 conventional von Klitzing constant R_K-90
items.explanation: This CIPM 1988 conventional value was used from 1990 for practical resistance representations; it is historical and is not the current exact SI value of R_K.

observationStage.conclusion: After the revised SI took effect on 20 May 2019, fixed h and e made the ideal K_J and R_K relationships exact in SI. The former K_J-90 and R_K-90 values remain useful historical comparison points, not current substitutions, while device realizations still require uncertainty evaluation.

guidedBlocks.title: Two fixed anchors support a network of exact identities
body: The present SI fixes h and e exactly. Algebra then makes K_J = 2e/h and R_K = h/e^2 exact current SI relationships.
The same anchors give the conductance quantum G_0 = 2e^2/h, the superconducting flux quantum Phi_0 = h/(2e), and the exact joule value 1 eV = e J.
These equations connect quantity values and units. They do not by themselves report how accurately a laboratory device realizes voltage or resistance.
guidedBlocks.sourceRevision: BIPM SI Brochure, 9th edition, 2026 update; CODATA 2022 adjustment
guidedBlocks.sourceLocator: Fixed h and e and exact derived electrical relationships
caveats: G_0 includes the conventional factor of two associated with spin degeneracy.

guidedBlocks.title: An exact relation and a practical realization answer different questions
body: A Josephson device can connect frequency and voltage, and a quantum Hall device can support resistance realization under specified operating conditions.
The ideal constants in the equations are exact in the current SI. A practical realization still has device conditions, corrections, traceability, and an uncertainty budget.
The network therefore labels exact identities separately from computed input values, historical conventional values, and practical realization claims.

technicalBlocks.title: The 1990 conventional values are comparison records, not current constants
body: The CIPM adopted conventional values K_J-90 = 483 597.9 GHz V^-1 and R_K-90 = 25 812.807 ohm for use from 1 January 1990 in practical electrical metrology.

They were exact by convention for those practical representations but did not equal the then-SI constants by definition. The revised SI replaced this arrangement by fixing h and e, so current K_J and R_K follow exactly from 2e/h and h/e^2.
The activity reports signed relative differences as (conventional - current exact SI)/current exact SI and never silently substitutes a 1990 value into the current network.

caveats: Historical conventional exactness and present SI exactness have different definitional contexts.

technicalBlocks.title: Carrier count is only a calculator input
body: For integer N, the calculator forms the charge magnitude q = N e and, when voltage V is supplied, the energy magnitude E = N e V.
In the Josephson view, a supplied V can be mapped by f = K_J V. This ideal conversion remains separate from junction step index, irradiation details, and practical realization uncertainty.
N is not a Hall filling factor, a conductance-channel count, or evidence that a quantized plateau has been realized.

caveats: Charge sign and device dynamics are outside the calculator.

equationSteps.label: Josephson constant and ideal conversion
equationSteps.explanation: Fixed h and e make K_J exact in the present SI; applying f = K_J V is an ideal device relationship, not a complete realization uncertainty statement.
equationSteps.sourceRevision: BIPM SI Brochure, 9th edition, 2026 update; CODATA 2022 adjustment
equationSteps.sourceLocator: Josephson constant and practical voltage realization relationship
caveats: Real Josephson realization requires specified junction operation and traceability.

equationSteps.label: von Klitzing and conductance identities
equationSteps.explanation: These are exact present-SI relationships derived from fixed h and e; a resistance realization also requires a valid quantum Hall operating condition.
equationSteps.sourceRevision: BIPM SI Brochure, 9th edition, 2026 update; CODATA 2022 adjustment
equationSteps.sourceLocator: von Klitzing constant and conductance quantum relationships
caveats: The activity does not model a Hall plateau or filling factor.

equationSteps.label: Superconducting magnetic flux quantum
equationSteps.explanation: The exact identity uses the charge magnitude 2e associated with paired superconducting carriers.
equationSteps.sourceRevision: BIPM SI Brochure, 9th edition, 2026 update; CODATA 2022 adjustment
caveats: The identity does not model flux trapping or a specific superconducting device.

equationSteps.label: Charge and electron-volt energy
equationSteps.expression: q = N e; E = q V; 1 eV = e J
equationSteps.explanation: For an integer carrier count, the calculator forms a charge magnitude and voltage-dependent energy; at one volt and N = 1 the joule value is exactly e.
equationSteps.sourceLocator: Fixed elementary charge and electron-volt definition
caveats: The calculator reports magnitude and omits charge sign and device dynamics.

equationSteps.label: Historical comparison convention
equationSteps.expression: delta_X = (X_90 - X_SI)/X_SI, for X in {K_J, R_K}
equationSteps.explanation: The signed ratio compares each 1990 conventional value with its current exact SI relationship without merging their statuses.
equationSteps.sourceRevision: BIPM SI Brochure, 9th edition, 2026 update; CODATA 2022 adjustment; CIPM 1988 conventional values effective 1990
equationSteps.sourceLocator: CIPM Recommendations 1 and 2 (CI-1988) historical comparison layer
caveats: The sign convention is conventional minus current, divided by current.
